textbookText: 8. Which group of modern periodic table is shown in the given table? What is the name given for metals in this group? Give reasons. What happens to the chemical reactivity while going top to bottom in this group? Why?
Group Be Mg
Ans:- The given table represents Group 2 (IIA) of the modern periodic table. The metals of this group are known Ca
as alkaline earth metals, such as Beryllium (Be), Magnesium (Mg), Calcium (Ca) and Strontium (Sr). These
Sr
elements are placed in the same group because each of them has two electrons in their outermost shell, which
gives them similar chemical properties. The chemical reactivity of these metals increases from top to bottom in the group.
This is because the atomic size increases and the valence electrons are held less strongly by the nucleus, so electrons can be
lost more easily.
9. Answer the following questions according to electronic configuration of given elements:
i) Write the name of the compound formed, molecular formula and type of chemical bond formed by the combination of

these two elements. Ans:- From the electronic configurations, element A is Carbon (C) (1𝑠2, 2𝑠22𝑝2) and element B is Oxygen (O) (1𝑠2, 2𝑠22𝑝4). When these two elements combine, they form carbon dioxide. The molecular formula of the compound is
CO₂. The chemical bond formed between carbon and oxygen is a covalent bond, because both elements share electrons to
complete their octet.
ii) Write down the balanced chemical equation when the above formed compound is dissolved in water.
Ans:- When carbon dioxide is dissolved in water, it forms carbonic acid.
CO2 + H2𝑂 → H2CO3 (Carbonic acid)
iii) Write down the group, period and block of element ‘A’ in periodic table.
Ans:- Element A (carbon) belongs to Group 14, Period 2, and the p-block of the modern periodic table.

ii) Which is more reactive between ‘b’ and ‘c’, why?
Ans:- Between b (chlorine) and c (bromine), chlorine (b) is more reactive. This is because in the halogen group, chemical
reactivity decreases from top to bottom due to increase in atomic size and decrease in the tendency to gain an electron.
